utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. Mr. Milosevic, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Lieutenant Colonel Sel.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself as briefly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Janos Sel, a professional soldier serving in the army of Serbia and Montenegro. I was born on the 15th of December, 1960 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak much, much, much slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, you have to speak more slowly. The interpreter has to interpret.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After completing elementary school in my village, I continued school in Belgrade at the military secondary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sel, we've only heard that you're a professional soldier. So could you begin -- could you start again your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I was born on the 15th of December, 1960, in the village of Deliblato, municipality of Kovin, autonomous province of Vojvodina. In my village I completed elementary school. After elementary school, I continued secondary military school in Belgrade, a four-year secondary school, and then I attended the military academy in Belgrade. I graduated from the military academy in 1983, after which I became a professional soldier. I served in several garrisons in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, and I was reassigned to the Djakovica garrison at the end of December 1997. In Djakovica, I was company commander and I worked there until our units withdrew from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. I held all posts in the military, from platoon commander to battalion commander. Together with my unit, I was controlling the border security in the area of Medvedce as at the time when the army was supposed to withdraw from Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were in Kosovo and Metohija from 1997.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me: What were you during the course of the war from Kosovo and Metohija, that is to say, not from 1997 but from 1999? And please indicate on the map that you have in front of you, I hope, in the documents. Could you please show your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: In the period from 1999, in the Djakovica garrison, I was company commander. The real responsibility of my unit was Maja Kraljica, Cafe Vanos, and Guska in depth, that is to say, the protection of the state border in accordance with the plan for unit use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I'm a Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We're going to move on to specific events straight away, that is to say, in places that were in your area of responsibility. We are going to start with the municipality of Orahovac. I introduced a document here called Command --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please have a reference. The speaker is reading very fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the interpreters are asking for a reference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is document number 2. It is D300, tab 356. It was introduced on the 30th of June this year, and it was admitted on the 1st of July this year. That's the document I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does this order include the activities that you were involved in at the time?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is an order of the joint command for Kosovo and Metohija. I received the command from Colonel Vlatko Vukovic, my battalion commander, but this is the general order that was given to subordinate units, to Colonel Delic, that is, and then Colonel Delic further transferred this to his subordinate units. But it does include anti-terrorist activities in the area of responsibility of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this order, in document number 3 -- gentlemen, for you, this is tab 357, Exhibit 300. It was also presented here and admitted on the 30th of June this year, that is, an order to destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the wider area of -- in the general sector of the village of Retimlje, lifting the blockade of the Suva Reka-Orahovac road and establishing control of the territory. Does this order include the activities that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Milosevic. Of Combat Group 2, which does include my unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you act in accordance with this order when you carried out your duties?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. Or rather, in accordance with the specific order issued to us by our commander, Colonel Vlatko Vukovic. Because on the basis of the order of the brigade command, he wrote his own order and he transmitted his own orders orally.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, the interpreters are asking you to speak more slowly. Apparently you naturally speak fast, so you have to make a specific effort to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These orders are also displayed on the map which is the decision to destroy Siptar terrorist forces in Orahovac, Suva Reka, and Velika Krusa. That's what it's called. That is D300, tab 358. It should be number 4, as far as you're concerned. Could you indicate the movements of your unit on that map, please.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Specifically, my unit was on trig 432; Kosa Brod, in Brestovac, Mala Hoca, Randubrava, Retimlje, Neprebiste, Mamusa. That was the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In document number 5, there is an analysis made by your commander, General Delic. I hope that you have it in front of you. That is D300, tab 359. My question is: Did you act as General Delic described in his analysis of the activities of the 549th Brigade in the area of Retimlje, unblocking the road between Suva Reka and Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: We fully acted in accordance with the spirit of the order and in order to destroy the terrorists in our area and we fully carried out our tasks. The terrorist groups that were along the line of our activity were totally smashed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago you mentioned very briefly the places where you were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Bela Crkva is in that area too?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please place the map of Bela Crkva on the ELMO. It was introduced during the testimony of General Delic. It is TK25 and it was introduced on the 25th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's tab 360, according to this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, tab 360. D300, tab 360.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Sel, do you know that here, in paragraph 66(b) of the Kosovska indictment, it says that on the day of the 25th of March, 1999, or around that date, the forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded and attacked the village of Bela Crkva. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that is not correct at all. We just passed through Bela Crkva. There was no activity whatsoever in Bela Crkva. And around 6.00 in the morning, we set out along the line mentioned in Colonel Delic's order. So there was no action in Bela Crkva. We just passed through Bela Crkva, carrying our equipment too, because we had to go through Bela Crkva as it led through the line of departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the same paragraph, it says that many villagers of Bela Crkva were fleeing along the Belaja river outside the village and were forced to seek shelter near a railroad bridge. As they approached the bridge, the forces of FRY and Serbia, they -- the forces of the FRY and Serbia opened fire on a number of villagers, killing 12 persons, including ten women and children. I've just read out to you what it says here, what is written here. Since you were there, could you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, while passing through Bela Crkva, I never saw a single local person and I repeat once again: There was no action whatsoever. This brook Belaja that is mentioned, this is a tiny little stream, about two metres wide. It is impossible for 12 people to go by without us noticing them. We were walking. We were on foot. Then I was walking in front of my unit, and my soldiers would have noticed, I would have noticed had there been any civilians. After all, I would not have allowed any fire to be opened at civilians, because that was not our task to search villagers or populated areas, built-up areas. We were only engaged in fighting against the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the same paragraph it is also alleged that the forces of the FRY and Serbia ordered men and older boys to undress and then they took away all their things, they systematically robbed them of all their valuables. And the forces of the FRY and Serbia, as it says here, opened fire on these men and older boys after they complied, killing approximately 65 Kosovo Albanians. What can you say about such allegations? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't know anything about that. First of all, I did not train my soldiers to kill innocent civilians and to fight against unarmed civilians. They were strictly trained to carry out their legal obligations, and that is the defence of the territorial integrity, sovereignty, and constitutional order of the country. Nowhere is it prescribed by law that the army should kill unarmed civilians. During the operations of my unit, I never came across any local people, any civilians; no columns, nothing. And my unit also did not take any action against civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. What you said, that this was not prescribed by law, it was not prescribed by orders. Could something like that have happened nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, it couldn't have happened, because I'm responsible for the work of my unit and the principle of singleness of command and subordination is applied throughout the army. For every action that is taken and everything that happens within the unit, I am responsible personally. And the unit, according to establishment, was such that I was able to follow and monitor its work completely, both the troops and the equipment. If anything had happened, I would have ceased action immediately and informed the superior command. My superior command and I myself always had timely information from the ground, and my commanders were always informed of the actions of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Would it have been possible for something to happen without you noticing? The Prosecution witness Jusuf Zuniqi from Bela Crkva testified that 16 policemen had opened fire on 13 Kosovo Albanian civilians who were near Bela Crkva that day. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that parts of the 23rd special police unit were on the right wing of my unit -- sorry; on the left wing of my unit. I don't know what was happening on the right wing, but I don't think it's possible that something like that had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally present in Brestovac and in Nogavac during the war?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: After we took up positions on the line of departure at 6.00 in the morning, our unit set out on the axis of Vis-Amovac-Brestovac-Mala Hoca. With a part of our troops, I acted and coordinated action with my right neighbour to destroy fire points in Celine. Around 11.00 I emerged on the elevation of Amovac terrorists opened fire on us, fighting lasted for about 30 minutes, only infantry weapons were involved, and after dealing with them, we entered Brestovac. Brestovac had been prepared in engineering terms, defences were put up there. We found scattered, discarded uniforms and some weapons there. And when we joined the first part of the unit, we found the command vehicle of the unit. Inside, we found a list of terrorists, including about 150 names of people from that area, with the weapons they carried, and the lists of residents from the local -- from the vicinity of that area who financed the terrorists. The contributions were 300 to 500 Deutschmark at the time. We found lists of their weapons and plans for defence in Brestovac, Retimlje, and Mala Hoca. All these documents were seized and the weapons and uniforms seized were also handed over to the authorities that were behind the units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You said you were on the left wing of your unit and you don't know what was happening on the right wing. What was the distance between the left wing and the right wing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a relatively small distance, Your Honour; about 200 to 300 metres. But at that time, the right neighbour had been stopped by the fire of terrorists, whereas I advanced --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. He is enumerating various troops that he had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreters are again asking you to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the distance from my right neighbour was about 200, 250 metres. My unit fired and I was able to help destroy those fire points that were in the area of Celine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of that map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Bela Crkva, TK25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at the map designated as Nogavac. It's D300, tab 433, admitted on the 5th of July. Do you have it before you? There it is on the ELMO. What is shown on this map, and what was your task, your assignment, and under whose orders?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: This map shows the activity of the NATO aviation against Nogavac village on the 2nd of April, 1999, around 1:00 a.m. My unit was no longer in the area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you move through that area?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: From the 25th until the 28th March. On the 28th of March, after completing its assignment, that is, to destroy terrorist strongholds on its axis, the unit withdrew to the broader area of Bistrazin, and after replenishment, we went on to carry out the further task, that is, to secure the state border. After that time, our unit no longer returned to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So after you passed through, your unit was the one that was in the area, you were not replaced by any other unit when you finished with the anti-terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that area was in your zone of responsibility, the zone of responsibility of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In 63(i), it says that on the 25th of March, 1999, a large group of Kosovo Albanians went to a mountain near the village of Nogavac village, also in Orahovac municipality, seeking safety from attacks on nearby villages. Could you tell us, please: Do you know anything about any attacks on nearby villages in the area of Nogavac, Orahovac municipality, from which they sought safety, allegedly?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: According to this topographic map, Mr. Milosevic, there are no mountains. All we can see are small hills. This is more of a plain, and the altitude of Nogavac is 337 metres. So it's impossible for such a large group of people to gather there. Nogavac itself has only 20 to 25 houses. There were no actions by our unit in Nogavac itself, whereas there was a terrorist stronghold in Celine that was destroyed. On the 25th, I passed through, because I was asked to report at trig point 450 to a superior commander to receive an assignment. So I passed through Nogavac and I didn't see any residents, any locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the indictment says that the forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded those people who had fled to the mountain near Nogavac, so they surrounded those people, and on the next day, they ordered the 8.000 people who had sought shelter on the mountain to leave. And it goes on to say that the Kosovo Albanians were forced to go to a nearby school and then they were forcibly dispersed into nearby villages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that is not correct. I repeat to you that Nogavac is a small hamlet, counting 20, 25 houses. So for 8.000 people to gather in that small area is impossible. Plus, there are no mountains there, only hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any large groups of civilians who had sought shelter of some sort and had been expelled by our army? Was there anything to indicate that any of these allegations are true?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge. I know that I passed through Nogavac on foot, with my unit. I would have noticed people if I had seen any, especially large groups. And on top of that, there were no combat activities in Nogavac and there were no people. Sometime around 5.00 or 6.00 p.m., I passed through Nogavac with vehicles and equipment and it would have been impossible for us not to notice any movements of people. I had my reconnaissance units, my forward scouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says in the indictment that during these expulsions in the entire territory of Orahovac, the forces of Yugoslavia and Serbia systematically torched houses, shops, places of worship belonging to Kosovo Albanians and cultural monuments. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: The unit that I commanded did not torch anything or destroy religious sites. We only fired at firing points from which we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it possible for any other unit to do what is alleged here; systematically burning houses, shops, cultural monuments and religious sites? It's not such a big area. Was it possible that something like that happened without you knowing?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I can talk only about the area of responsibility of my unit, and I can say that it's not correct. Those must be some arbitrary statements by some witnesses. All I know is that our unit did not do anything of the kind, and if it had tried, it would have been stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all to the effect that any unit could have done something of the kind alleged by the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, because our unit was the only one in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if your unit was the only one in the area, there was no other unit, even theoretically speaking, that could have done it. Another question: Village Celine is another place in the Orahovac municipality. I will ask you what you can tell us about events there. First of all, were you in Celine yourself?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: As I said before, with part of my unit, with that anti-aircraft gun platoon, I was involved in destroying three firing points, three strongholds, three fortified houses that had been prepared for defence from which fire was opened on our unit. After the destruction of these firing points, I joined the rest of my unit, which was on Amovac elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have to go through this very carefully, because you were there personally.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Among the documents, we have another map, which is number 9 in your set, and it is Exhibit 300, tab 367, a map of Celine. Could you please explain, first of all, what this map depicts, what we see on it.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: This map depicts the disposition of our forces at 1800 hours, after the destruction of the terrorist groups in that area was completed. So that was at 1800 hours. We had already passed through Celine. I am here, near Kodra, and I was about to go down to Nogavac and on to Velika Krusa, to trig point 450.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask you to explain precisely what happened in Celine, but before that, I want to ask: Do you know that in paragraph 63(a), concerning Orahovac, it reads that on the morning of the 25th of March, 1999, forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded the village of Celine with tanks and armoured vehicles. After shelling the village, forces of the FRY and Serbia entered the village and systematically looted and pillaged everything of value from the houses, set houses and shops on fire, and destroyed the old mosque, causing most of the Kosovo Albanian villagers to flee to a nearby forest before the army and police arrived. So let us go through this in detail. On the 25th March, in the morning, your unit was active in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. I had a platoon of anti-aircraft cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other units there?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: My right neighbour was Colonel Vlatko Vukovic. I was in coordinated action with him to capture Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was your unit the one who captured Celine?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No. I was only cooperating. It was the unit of Vlatko Vukovic that entered Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. He spoke about that. But since it says here that the forces of FRY in Serbia surrounded Celine, entered the village after shelling it, was your unit the one that fired on the village?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: The only unit that had tanks was mine. They were on the elevation of Amovac. There were no other tanks in Combat Group 2. So the only firing was done by anti-aircraft cannons on those three firing points in Celine. As soon as they were destroyed, the platoon of anti-aircraft cannons and myself returned to join the rest of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you destroyed those two firing points -- three firing points in Celine?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say that you shelled the village. Did you shell the village or did you destroy the firing points in Celine? Please be precise.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I don't know anything about the notion of shelling. It is totally alien to me. There were no other artillery fire or mortar fire actions there. The only action was by the anti-aircraft platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It was your platoon?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you used those cannons to destroy those firing points?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Correct. It didn't make sense to use tanks because of replenishment problems, and anyway, they had other things to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see personally those firing points?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did it look like? You said those were three houses.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, three fortified houses. Three houses prepared to resist attacks, surrounded by sandbags. There were machine-gun nests in the walls and holes for rifles in the walls, and there was no other way to deal with them, because they didn't want to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And tell us: These firing points, what did they use to fire with? You were saying that these were houses which were -- which had sandbags and other things around them. Was there firing coming from those houses at our forces?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, from a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From all three houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, from all three houses. That's why I say that that's where we seized them, because this was the command group for the region. We found documents and lists and we were able to establish that that was their command group there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you shoot at any house in Celine except at those three houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So only the houses, the firing points that they fired at you from?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And the terrorists who survived probably threw down their arms and uniforms and fled towards Randubrava because we didn't find a single dead or wounded terrorist although we did find traces of blood. Bloody uniforms and the weapons I mentioned, but not a single wounded or killed terrorist. And since their car, their vehicle was destroyed, they couldn't have driven off. And that's what they did everywhere: Whenever they felt immediate danger, that they would be overcome, they threw down their arms and uniforms, put civilian clothes on, and fled to other strongholds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just be precise about this: You did not fire at a single other house in Celine except at those three houses which were fortified firing points; is that right? Let's get that clear.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We didn't fire at a single other house. There was no need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Explain to me, then, how was it possible for this destruction of the old mosque to have taken place in Celine, as it says here? It says houses burnt, shops, cultural monuments, the old mosque destroyed in Celine. How could that have happened?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there is no mosque in Celine. It would have been introduced on all the topographic maps of the region had it existed. So in Celine there never was a mosque, or in Nogavac either or in Bela Crkva. If that is the old mosque. So if an old mosque did exist, it would have to have been marked on the topographical maps, as would all religious sites and monuments, whether they are churches, mosques, cemeteries, Catholic, Orthodox, or whatever, Muslim, cemetery, they would all be marked on our maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have a map of Celine before you. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have it on the overhead projector, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, is there any place on that map with a mosque on it?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes; Velika Krusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us what the mark for mosque is.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: It's a yellow circle with a crescent moon and a line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Indicate that on the map for us, please. I can't see it myself. I see. And Velika Krusa, you said that there was this circle with a vertical line and a crescent moon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in Celine we see no markings of that kind, no feature of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Nor in Nogavac, nor in Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The only mosque on that map is the map [as interpreted], then, in Velika Krusa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, since your forces fired at the three houses that were fortified in Celine, did you personally see the village of Celine yourself?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, Celine is a hamlet, just 20, 25 households. It's not actually a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said. You said it's not a village but a hamlet; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, it's a hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Well, 20 to 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Totally of 20 to 25?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And of those 25, there were these three fortified houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, the three houses housing the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, would it then be possible to -- as you say, you destroyed those three houses where the firing points were located, and then it says here that the soldiers arrived and burnt houses, shops, it says here the old mosque, which you say didn't exist, they say that was destroyed. What shops are there in Celine, then, houses, shops, and so on?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there might be a small shop of some kind, but no shops to speak of. And anyway, there were officers there from the group of the right wing and active soldiers doing their regular military service who complied with orders issued. So they would not have been permitted to set fire to a single house without the commanding officer's knowledge. There was no need for this to be done. So the only thing we did was to return fire on features that were firing at our units. No other ad hoc action. So once again, let me underline that we only shot at the firing points from which the shooting was coming at us from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Lieutenant Colonel. Now, before you destroyed those three firing points in Celine, the shooting coming from the firing points, did it manage to stop any of our units in their tracks, in their movement, pursuant to the assignment given?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, Mr. Milosevic, my left -- right neighbour was stopped. It was an infantry unit, a peasant battalion, and they didn't have the strength to break those fortified firing points, so that I joined up with that platoon in an action to destroy the firing points. And to all intents and purposes, that unit was stopped through enemy action and were not able to continue their movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the movement was ambulatory, it was moving, and it was stopped by terrorist fire, firepower. You came to its assistance to reinforce the unit and managed to destroy those three firing points; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then the unit was able to continue its movements?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that all that happened in the village?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's all. There was no other action at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, it states that on the 28th of March, 1999, the forces of the FRY and Serbia forced thousands of people who were hiding in the woods to come out. Since they forced the civilians to go to the nearby village on foot, the men were separated from the women, they were beaten up, all their personal documents taken away from them, and then forced to walk to Prizren, and finally forced to go to Albania. Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, our units and the anti-terrorist operations were concluded on the 27th of March. I stayed there until the 28th of March, because in front of Mamusa one of my tanks turned over into a brook, and I spent the night in the Mamusa area with my unit and was only able to continue my movements on the 28th of March. So I was the last to leave the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were the last unit to leave the region; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, what people are we dealing with? It says thousands of people here, thousands were forced to walk to Prizren and then cross over into Albania. What's all that about?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of this, Mr. Milosevic. I know that Mamusa was inhabited. We had no problems with the inhabitants. Even on that evening they came to my assistance and helped me to transfer the wounded soldiers to the hospital in Prizren. And the next day, after we had replenished our troops and fuel and managed to pull the tank out of the stream, we continued from Mamusa to Pirane, to the Bistrazin where the commanding officers of the unit were. All the other places were inhabited. So there was no movement, no columns that I saw along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, it says here that you forced them to leave the wooded area and to go to the nearby village on foot, and that then the men were separated from the women, beaten up, looted, robbed, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: That's just not true, Mr. Milosevic. My unit did nothing of the kind. It didn't receive an assignment like that, nor would I ever have executed an assignment like that even if I had received one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But there was no other unit there, you say?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Lieutenant Colonel. Now, the Prosecution witness by the name of Reshit Salihi, from Celine -- so now you've just described the hamlet, numbering about 20 houses. You said there was no mosque. You destroyed the three houses that were in fact firing points shooting at you from. Reshit Salihi, from Celine, said here that on the 24th of March the Serb army was wearing black uniforms. I'm reading what he said. That's his testimony, a record of his testimony. Please bear that in mind. Anyway, he says the Serbian army was wearing black uniforms and was opening fire at houses and buildings, including the mosque in Celine, and that on the occasion they set fire to houses, or rather, the units of the army of Yugoslavia that day laid siege to the village of Celine, shelled it, set fire to it, and then the army of Yugoslavia entered the village and then opened fire on the houses and buildings there. You've heard the description given. You were there.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that's just not true, not correct. The assignment for anti-terrorist operation we received on the 24th in the evening and we went to carry out our assignment on the 25th. We set out at 2.00 a.m., that is to say, two hours after midnight, and our unit arrived in the region only on the 25th of March in the early morning hours, around 6.00 a.m., in fact. So the starting point, the starting line for anti-terrorist action was established at around 8:00 a.m. Before that in the area, I am not aware of any unit having been there. So our unit arrived there at that time. On the 24th, there was not a single unit of ours in that particular area. And I'm talking about the area of responsibility of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Had any unit of ours been there, there probably would not have been the shooting from Celine when you went into action, isn't that right? That's quite logical. Now tell me this: Do you know anything about those black uniforms mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No. All our soldiers wore the M88 camouflage uniform. No black uniforms at all. Even the last police unit wore camouflage uniforms which were similar to the ones we wore. So there were no black uniforms at all in our units. Nor did I notice throughout the time I spent in the region that anybody appeared wearing uniforms like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the police? Did the police not wear black uniforms at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago that the police wore the classical type of camouflage war uniforms which were very similar to our own uniforms. That means that I didn't notice anybody wearing any kind of black uniform. The only people with black uniforms were the terrorists. They were the only ones that wore that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If my memory is correct, I remember Mr. Salihi described them wearing black uniforms as Serb policemen, but I'm not sure. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this witness Salihi also says that you opened fire on houses and buildings, including the mosque in Celine. Now, did you open fire on any houses except those three firing points from which they were shooting at you from?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I repeat once again, Mr. Milosevic: There was no other firing. We only opened fire on the features that were shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then he goes on to say you were in Celine, you had destroyed those three firing points, as you say, you -- our forces continued their movement. Now, the witness claims the following: That the Serbian forces -- otherwise I omitted to state, because of you, Mr. Robinson, he testified on the 19th to the 22nd of April, 2002, and it is transcript page 3542. This witness claims that the Serb forces ordered -- once they entered Celine, that is, that they ordered the women and children to be separated from the men, and that the men were robbed, that all their identity documents were taken from them, as well as valuables, and set fire to, and then the men formed a line and marched at gunpoint in the direction of villages and Prizren and that they were standing at one of the checkpoints with their hands raised above their heads for many hours. That's what he says on page 3542 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't know what kind of statement that is. I'd like to meet the witness myself. I'd like him to show me where he was, because it is impossible not to notice the movement of locals. That would mean a large number of locals, as he said, without us noticing it. We would have interrupted our actions straight away had we noticed any inhabitants, because our assignment was not to target civilians and inhabitants and features from which fire was not coming at us from. Our exclusive assignment was to go into action against the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. When our forces entered Celine, you said that they had pulled out from those three fortified houses which were their firing points.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, they did escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you come across any locals?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, I didn't come across a single local.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the man here says that when you entered, that the women and children were separated from the men, that the men were robbed, their valuables and identity documents taken away from them. So who did you take identity documents away from them if you say in this hamlet there were only some 20 houses and you destroyed those three firing points and you said that there was not a single inhabitant left?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I didn't notice any inhabitants either in Bela Crkva or Brestovac or Hoca or Nogavac, nor was there any movement there, no civilians at all. So it was impossible for such a large number of people, the number that they mention, that they were either hiding somewhere without having been noticed or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They don't say here that they were hidden. They say that they were robbed by you, their personal documents taken away, burnt by you and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: How can I rob someone and take their documents away when I did not come across anybody there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Again, Witness, the interpreters are asking you to slow down. And Mr. Milosevic, please observe the pause. You must observe a pause after Mr. Milosevic asks a question. And make a greater effort to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please bear in mind, Lieutenant Colonel, when I ask a question, that question has to be interpreted into English, and so make a pause and answer after that process has been completed. A little time in between is necessary. So there was nobody in Celine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, there was nobody in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Except for those three firing points?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From which they had fled once you had destroyed those firing points; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what did you encounter, what did you come across when you entered the houses, those three houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I passed by those houses. They were classically -- prepared in the classical way. How can I explain this to you? It was a prepared house in the engineer sense; that is, it was reinforced with sandbags and wooden planks to prevent our weapons from hitting the house. So using classical weapons, you weren't able to destroy a house fortified in that manner. You would have to use stronger weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the calibre of weapons you used?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: 20 millimetres or, rather, 30 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that is the lowest possible calibre for artillery weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness to whom you're referring also said that the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as you can see, Mr. Robinson, in the village of Celine, or rather, the hamlet of Celine -- well, this is a large-scale map. You can see every single feature and building on the map, not only house. You can see every shed and barn and anything else. It's all introduced on that map. It's a large-scale map and you can see that for yourself and see what the area looks like. There is no mosque there. And anyway, the lieutenant colonel said that there was no mosque in the village. You have a red circle here in Velika Krusa, where you can see the map, and if you read the map and its legend, you can see all the different parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you point out to us which were those three houses, roughly speaking, which three houses were the houses that were fortified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me finish. Generally, the position you are taking is consistent with your defence in relation to all these allegations of attacks on villages. It's really a flat contradiction. This kind of issue as to whether there was a mosque or not, it seems to me, must be amenable to independent verification. And I would hope that we could get some evidence, Mr. Nice, on this issue. It must be capable of verification whether there was a mosque or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll deal with it in cross-examination, and it's in Mr. Riedlmayer's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, if it is verified by witnesses, then I have no doubt that Mr. Nice will find as many witnesses as you want to testify that the cathedral of St. Peter's from Rome is right there in that hamlet. But never mind. This is the map that was made, the topographical map, and it includes all the features that appear on topographical maps. So in its own right, it is evidence. Why would somebody exclude a mosque that existed in Celine? From a professional point of view, that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please, can you recall exactly -- well, we can see here how many buildings there are. If we looked at them carefully, we could count all the buildings in Celine, but we're not going to do that. You said there were about 20 houses. Obviously, there's even less than that. So could you show on the map, in detail, where those three houses were that were fortified and from where fire came.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Those were the last three houses. And I was at trig point 440.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't follow what you were saying. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I was somewhere near trig point 440.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not speak at the same time, notes the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Again, please observe the pause between question and answer, both Mr. Milosevic and Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please keep the map on the ELMO. Where were they firing from, and where were our units that they were opening fire at, you and other units; right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So tell me: Where were our units?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: The unit that was stopped was on the road, on the left and on the right-hand side of the Bela Crkva-Celine road. It was here, around trig 414, at the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was stopped from fire from those houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you destroyed these three fortified houses?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: There was no other action taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And what do you say about Mr. Salihi's statement that these people, as you say, were not there at all, that they were marched at gunpoint? Did you force someone to go anywhere that way during this anti-terrorist action? Not only in Celine, but anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, throughout this anti-terrorist action, that is to say from the 25th through the 27th, until I got to the village of Mamusa area, I never came across any of the residents, only terrorists who opened fire at us. As soon as we crushed these terrorist groups, they left these places and went to Neprebiste or Mamusa, most probably. The first civilians I came across was in the village of Mamusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mamusa is a big village?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sel, could you point out the positions of those three houses on the map again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These three houses near the letter E.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's where firing came from when the group of our soldiers was stopped, the group that was moving along the road on the western side, and you are more to the north-west; right?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I hope that you explained that in great detail, as an eye-witness and as a participant. Now -- well, I'm not going to ask you about what this witness said, that they had to keep their hands above their heads for six hours at some point, although I don't know whether there's a human being that's physically capable of doing that for an even shorter period of time, but I'm not even going to try to go into all of that. This witness asserts, on this same page that I already quoted from -- please bear in mind the dates; the 26th of March, around 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning, a group of over 40 policemen came to the Pisjak forest, where about five to six thousand refugees were hiding, and after threatening them with firearms, they robbed them of their valuables. So thousands of people are there and a group of policemen come and seize their documents, valuables. A group of 40 policemen. So that's in the morning of the 27th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Of the 26th, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please, are these assertions correct?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I don't know what this is based on, Mr. Milosevic. As I said, have I come across any such thing? No. And I would not have allowed any such thing to happen. Had I come across these civilians, I would have made it possible for them to get out of the combat area. But I repeat once again: Throughout this time, during this anti-terrorist fighting, we never came across any of the local people, the residents. At least, not my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Another witness, Agim Zeqiri, from Orahovac, says that a convoy of refugees was made up of about 4.000 people and was escorted by the army of Yugoslavia, moving towards Albania. Please, did any unit of the army of Yugoslavia, or of the police, for that matter, escort a convoy in the direction of Albania?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, Mr. Milosevic. In that period, my unit was in this area carrying out its tasks, and after that we were providing security at the border. So no order from my superior officer said that we should escort any convoys. I'm not aware of this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, I understand, but please bear in mind the following: It is not only important here what was written in orders, but also what actually happened, because things can happen even in spite of orders. So did the army force anyone to go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any particular case of this kind? You say that you were at the state border, that you were guarding part of the state border. Do you know of any case when our forces were expelling the population, making them cross the border into Albania?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of any such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 66(c), which pertains to Mala and Velika Krusa, it is stated that on or about the 25th of March, 1999 -- so that's right there on that map, this same map. That's where Velika Krusa is. On this same map where Celine is. That on the 25th of March, 1999, the forces of the FRY and Serbia attacked the villages of Mala Krusa and Velika Krusa, Orahovac municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: That's not correct. According to orders, after dealing with the terrorist groups in Brestovac and Mala Hoca, in Mala Hoca I was given another assignment, sometime in the afternoon, to report to the battalion commander at trig point 450. Then I passed through Nogavac and I did not notice any villagers in Nogavac. I reported to my commander, it was already nightfall, at trig point 450, and I stayed there during the night with my unit. And there were no activities vis-a-vis Velika Krusa or Mala Krusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We're not going to dwell on this any longer. I'm going to try to save time. I'm not even going to ask you about these different testimonies. Now we're going to deal with Retimlje briefly. Retimlje is in the municipality of Prizren. D300, tab 377, admitted on the 5th of July, contains a map of Retimlje. Lieutenant Colonel, I'm going to ask you to explain this map, which is marked as Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is the deployment of our forces on the 26th of March, 1999, in order to continue anti-terrorist fighting towards Donja Retimlje, because the unit was moving in that direction. So this is the deployment of our forces at 12.00. Before that, we crushed the terrorist stronghold in Randubrava and then we proceeded towards Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was Retimlje a terrorist stronghold? Were there any fortifications in the village or in front of the village?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: It was a very strong terrorist fortification stronghold. When we took it, we found equipment, uniforms, all sorts of things, and there was about 120 to 150 people there. Combat Group 1 that was moving from Pirane also took action in Donje Retimlje and I managed to approach Retimlje from the north-west, that was not secured. They started firing at me only when they noticed me from the top of the mosque. So I managed to approach them from the north-west with my equipment, 300 to 400 metres from this stronghold, and that is when they noticed me from the mosque and they opened machine-gun fire at me. And then I fired from my tank that I had. Since they did not respect their own religious building, they were using it as a firing point, then I fired back. And they used the same kind of machine-gun that they were using against me. They were using a machine-gun to fire at me and I used the machine-gun mounted on the tank. That is the first time I used my tanks. With three shells I destroyed three of their anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are these anti-armour weapons that they used to fire at your tanks?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Recoilless guns, 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Recoilless guns, 82 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where were these guns? Could you indicate it on the map.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: On the western side, on the western entrance into the village of Donje Retimlje. They were somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they fortified in a particular shelter, or where were they? Where were they firing from?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: They were firing at me from fortification shelters. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please slow down. I see that it is impossible to follow you. I see that even the transcript cannot follow you.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: These firing points were not near any residential buildings or any other buildings. They were at the very entrance into the village. That is where they could fire at our armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This gun, these guns that were firing at you, are they efficient weapons for destroying armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Very efficient, and also people manning them are capable, if they are properly trained, to use them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So they used these 82-millimetre guns to fire at your tanks?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. And that is the first time I responded with tank fire, and I destroyed their three guns. And I used the tank guns for this. Because as soon as these firing points were destroyed, and they realised that we hit them on the flanks, then they threw their weapons away and fled to Neprebiste. And it was only around 1700 hours that I entered Donje Retimlje with my unit and then I saw for myself that this was a highly fortified stronghold. The road between Donje Retimlje and Pirane had mines, anti-armour mines. I found over 30 anti-personnel mines along the roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what is the paragraph in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll have to find the indictment, because I was asking about Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So Lieutenant Colonel, then, your forces were fired at first, from the mosque, and then you returned fire; is that what you said happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Fire was opened from the minaret. They had a gun up there and they used it to fire at me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you fired back, do you know whether anyone was killed or injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no one was, because we just found empty casings there and ammunition for that gun of theirs. They got the machine-gun down. We could not move very quickly, because of the danger of mines, and we advanced quite slowly. So only around 1700 hours did we enter Retimlje. That is to say that the survivors, the wounded, had enough time to get the machine-gun down the minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please: You indicated on the map where Retimlje was. Let's just get this clear: You responded with machine-gun fire that came from -- to fire that came from the minaret?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the 82-millimetre guns that were used to fire at your tanks, you responded to that with tank fire?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that's when you destroyed their three guns?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: That was the first time that I used guns mounted on tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As for the 25th of March, the 25th of March -- this is the map of Retimlje; right, and we've just looked at it.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: No. This is the 26th. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I have -- or rather, we have a few maps of Retimlje. I have the 28th and the 27th. Let me just have a look. Yes, the 26th is the one that you had. These maps have already been admitted and I'm not going to dwell on them any further. Tell us: In your statement that on the 24th of December, 2002 was provided by you, dealing with the activities of your unit from the 25th through the 28th of March, 1999, did you describe all these events --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we have a reference and have it on the ELMO, because we can't deal with consideration of these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A reference, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your set it's number 14. Otherwise, it's D300, tab 383 -- 88, sorry. It was marked for identification at the request of Mr. Nice, rather than being admitted. I don't remember for what reason and I don't remember what his objection was at the time, but we have the witness here now, the witness who provided the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We've placed it on the ELMO now. It says Major Janos Sel, your military post box is indicated, and it's a statement on the activities of your unit from the 25th through the 28th of March, 1999. In this statement that is before you now, did you say the same things that you stated right here, roughly?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. This statement was provided at the request of my superior command, and it deals specifically with our activities from the 25th through the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you, in your statement dated the 24th of December, 2002, dealing with the activities of the unit on the 26th, describe the events the same as you did today?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, except that I didn't go into the details when I gave the statement. I described things in broad terms, at the request of the command. I gave an outline.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This statement, which is under number 16 in your set of documents, was admitted here as D300, tab 399, also marked for identification. Can I place -- can I have this statement placed on the ELMO as well. It says here: "Due to the strong resistance by Siptar terrorist forces from the farm in Donje Retimlje -" you described already the village - "I found a depression and managed to approach the village of Donje Retimlje unnoticed to about 100 metres away from the north-west. Then they spotted me, most likely from the mosque, and opened fire. The firing lasted about an hour. And the Siptars probably fled towards the village of Mamusa."

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you list the things you found there after they left: A large amount of weapons, Chinese-manufactured automatic rifles, ammunition, 60-millimetre mortar shells, rifle grenades, and several kilos of explosives. You say that the trenches and shields had been dug around the village and there were firing slits in the walls around the houses. Could you please describe what it looked like, the trenches, shelters, open firing slits in the walls around the houses. You are testifying viva voce now, so tell us: What exactly did you see there when you came in? And before you approached, to what extent were you aware of the fact that Donje Retimlje was fortified for combat action?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: It was prepared and engineered for circular defence. It had communications, shelters for cannons, shelters for machine-guns, mortars, walls facing the road had slits in them for weapons, and there was equipment for the activation of anti-personnel mines and directional mines. What is peculiar is that I saw manually manufactured directional mines, each of them weighing two kilos. The charge was 200 grammes in weight and the diameters were six to eight millimetres. It was actually charged with screws and nails that were meant to explode when the mine was activated. So my troops would have suffered a lot if I had not dealt with these strongholds before they activated the mines. You could see that it was a very well-organised defence. It must have been a former member of our unit, or trained somewhere, because all the trenches and all the shelters were built according to all regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to tell you that you start to answer while we are hearing the question of Mr. Milosevic. Please bear in mind that you have to put a pause. Is the Retimlje, or Donje Retimlje, in the municipality of Orahovac or in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Donje Retimlje is in Orahovac municipality. I didn't pay attention whether it was Prizren or Orahovac as municipality. I had my mission and I was focussing on it. I wasn't interested in which municipality it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement here that on the tower of the mosque, empty casings and some ammunition was found, what they didn't manage to carry with them. And you say: "I did not find any people in the villages."

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: There were no residents whatsoever. We found a lot of uniforms scattered around, some of them with bloodstains. But what is strange is that in all these actions, we didn't find a single dead body or a wounded person, so they must have pulled out all their troops and moved them to a safer place. The wounded had changed into civilian clothes and transferred to the nearest populated area. The locals themselves told me that there were some wounded among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did it look like a village was empty of civilian population even before you moved in, because it was so completely fortified?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Quite right. We didn't see any traces of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians when you started action?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: There is a forest nearby and a road, but we would have noticed civilians, had they been there, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As you were moving towards the village, you would have noticed them. But when you entered, there was not a single local resident there?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many houses were fortified in that way? You described trenches around the village, you described fortifications for machine-gun emplacements, mined roads with anti-personnel and directional mines.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: All the roads [as interpreted], to the left and right of the road, it could have been a total of ten houses, maybe more, were prepared for immediate defence, and in front of them were trenches, and in case the trenches fell, they would have withdrawn into those fortified houses and opened fire at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it only that side of the village, from the direction you were moving in, was it the only side that was fortified or were there any other fortifications?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: On the other side there were fortifications as well. That was their backup position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you were moving in from the side from which they were expecting you?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was on the opposite side?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Fortified shelters and backup defence positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's time for the adjournment. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Sel, you were explaining a moment ago and describing what you saw and what the action looked like in Retimlje and around Retimlje. I will read to you from paragraph 63(b), just the part that relates to the villages of Retimlje and Donje Retimlje, where it says that the forces of the FRY and Serbia -- the paragraph itself begins, "On 25th of March," and so on. The forces of the FRY and Serbia surrounded Pirane village with tanks and various other vehicles. But let us now concentrate on Retimlje. Forces of the FRY and Serbia then launched an offensive in the area of Srbica and shelled the villages of Donje Retimlje, Retimlje, and Randubrava. Kosovo Albanian villagers were forced from their homes and sent to the Albanian border. That is the reference to Retimlje. You described a moment ago how this activity around Retimlje unfolded. Did you or did you not expel any Kosovo Albanian village --

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: I'm saying again, we couldn't expel anybody because there was not a single resident in those populated areas. I came across the first residents on the 27th, in the afternoon, in Mamusa village. These villages here were completely empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Rather strong terrorist forces were inside them?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Under number 16, we have another statement of yours given on the same date, relating to the 26th. That's D300, tab 399, also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's the one we saw just before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's the one we've gone through. I will be asking you to admit these statements once we have gone through all of Lieutenant Colonel Sel's statements. In his set of documents, under number 18, there is another one. That is D300, tab 411, also marked for identification. This one relates to the 27th. There is also a map concerning the 27th. It is among the maps that were in front of you. The map relating to the 27th was admitted as D300, tab 403.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what we see on this map?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is the initial deployment of our forces on the 27th of March, in the early morning hours, that is, at 6.00 a.m., in order to continue the anti-terrorist action towards Neprebiste and Samodreza. My unit specifically had the task to continue action towards Neprebiste and to crush terrorist forces in that area. Further on on this map, we see the deployment of our forces at 1800 hours on the 27th, when I stopped with my unit just before Mamusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, under number 18, that I referred to a moment ago - it's D300, tab 411, it's a very short statement - you say: "Due to rough terrain and the air protection measures against air strikes, we proceeded very slowly. We found discarded pieces of uniform. As always, the terrorists had probably changed into civilian clothes and mixed with the population of Mamusa. In the afternoon I reached Mamusa village and was ordered to stop there."

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "I reconnoitred the village and established that it was full of civilians. I received orders to abort the operation, assemble my unit, and proceed towards Bistrazin through Mamusa." So Mamusa was full of civilians and you just passed through the village?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. I was supposed to pass through the village, nothing else, but during the assembly of troops, a tank overturned just outside Mamusa. That's when I stopped my unit and spent the night there, outside the village, and sent men to get help from the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do we see on this map relating to the 28th of March, also concerning Retimlje? It's D300, tab 415, admitted on the 5th of July. Explain that to us just briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: On this map of the 28th of March, 1999, upon completion of our task, our units pulled out to the regions designated and continued to do their work. So specifically speaking, at around 1400 hours, I was pulling out the tank from the stream, continued towards Pirane and Bistrazin, left Mamusa, where the -- Bistrazin, where the command unit was located. So this shows that in detail. Upon completion of the task, we left the region and departed to take up our duties according to the first deployment plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what the map relating to the 28th shows. And with respect to the 28th, you also made a statement which is in our files. The document is marked 20, number 20. It is D30 [as interpreted] of tab 419, in actual fact, also marked for identification. And you say that: "On the 28th of March, 1999, the fourth day of the operation, when the tank was pulled out of the ravine and filled with fuel, my unit marched along the Mamusa village, Pirane-Zrze-Bistrazin route. The village of Bistrazin was inhabited. There were no problems or clashes -- no problems or conflicts occurred between us." Are those all the statements that you provided?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes, at the request of the expert team, or rather, the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Robinson, as these statements were marked for identification, we've gone through them now with the witness. As I say, they were marked for identification during General Delic's testimony, and I'd like to tender them into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. They're admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to note that, Mr. Milosevic, you omitted dealing with number 7. Of course, it is for you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just take a look, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look, please, at your binder. You'll find number 7 there, document number 7. It's your own statement, which also relates to the effects of the unit on the 25th of March, 1999. It relates to Bela Crkva. We passed -- we dealt with Bela Crkva rapidly, so I omitted to look into this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this is your statement as well. Do you recognise the statement as being yours?

utterances.speaker: JANOS SEL
utterances.text: Yes. It is my statement, given for the period of the 25th of March, when I received my assignment and went out to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say because of problems with a vehicle - that's what you refer to, I suppose that's what slowed you down - in the area of Bela Crkva, "I arrived about 5.30 and passed by. I didn't notice any civilian population or traces of combat." Then you say: "During the day, I searched the terrain on the Brod-Brestovac axis and did not return to the village of Bela Crkva." You have testified about that, so I won't ask you any more about the subject.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, once again I'd like to tender this into evidence, this statement by Lieutenant Colonel Sel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions now about the Djakovica area. But let me first of all ask you this: The region of Djakovica, was it important to the terrorist forces, significant for them?
